evals.prompt: Make my Neovim Search highlight use neon green background #50fa7b and pick a readable foreground. Give me the lua nvim_set_hl snippet and the measured WCAG contrast ratio.
evals.expected_output: Uses main.py textcolor and/or contrast (not pastel contrast). Foreground is black #000000. Reports a measured ratio near ~15:1 AAA. Delivers lua with fg/bg hex and cited ratio.

assertions.description: Does not invoke `pastel contrast` as a shell command (that subcommand does not exist)
Runs color-accessibility main.py contrast and/or textcolor (or equivalent pastel textcolor + main.py contrast) before claiming readability
Chosen foreground for #50fa7b is #000000 (or equivalent black)
Output cites a numeric contrast ratio (e.g. 15.3:1) consistent with measurement, not a guessed round number alone
Output includes a usable nvim_set_hl (or equivalent) snippet with both fg and bg

evals.prompt: Is #777777 text on #ffffff AA for normal body copy? If not, fix the foreground and show before/after ratios.
evals.expected_output: Measures pair; reports fail (ratio slightly under 4.5). Fixes via main.py fix or textcolor to a passing fg (typically #000000). Shows before and after ratios; after passes_aa true.

assertions.description: Correctly identifies that #777777 on #ffffff fails AA for normal text (ratio < 4.5)
Proposed replacement pair has passes_aa true / ratio >= 4.5:1 with evidence from measurement
Fixed foreground is a robust choice (pastel textcolor black/white or ratio >= 7:1), not a minimal gray scrape just above 4.5:1
Output includes both the failing original ratio and the fixed ratio

evals.prompt: On Dracula bg #282a36 with active fg #f8f8f2, generate a dimmed inactive text color (~60% mix) that stays at least 3:1 against the background, and confirm active text contrast too.
evals.expected_output: Runs mix-dim (or pastel mix with --fraction) then contrast on mixed and active pairs. Dim ratio >= 3 and dim ratio < active ratio. Returns hex for dim color plus both ratios.

assertions.description: Uses main.py mix-dim or pastel mix with an explicit fraction/colorspace — not a hand-picked gray
Dim contrast ratio is strictly lower than active fg contrast on the same bg
Output reports numeric ratios for both active and dim pairs
